title: PROC 26-3490 Greenock Phase 1 - Ben Lomond View (BLV) refurbishment
description: The Authority wishes to appoint a contractor to deliver the works package for the refurbishment of Ben Lomond View, Pottery Street, Greenock Inverclyde, PA15 2UZ. Works must be completed by 30 April 2027. The existing Greenock Police Station was built c. 1970 and is key in providing operational policing to the community of the Inverclyde area. Over the past few decades, the use of the building has evolved, and alongside aspects due to general age of the building, and the roll out of various new systems, practices, and technologies, the current building no longer suits the requirements of 21st century policing. As such there is a need to exit the station and relocate the Police Station to another property at Ben Lomond View, Pottery Steet, Greenock. The intention is to refurbish Ben Lomond View, so it is fit for use for future years. The Authority is leasing the site from Riverside Inverclyde.

title: Evaluation of Rural Land Market Reporting
description: The aims of the project are to produce an evaluation of the SLCâs rural land market reporting to generate insights and improvements for future reporting. The evaluation will focus on several elements: 1) Impact â this objective is to understand the use of the report and its effects, outcomes and the extent to which reporting is effective in informing policy and decision making. There is a comparative element for this. 2) Process â understanding the effectiveness of the current approach, how the reporting process is working, assessing potential improvements to the methodology, and considering expansion of the coverage of reporting to other areas. 3) Economic Value â understanding value for money and costing the tangible benefits of the reports compared to the costs. What are the wider economic benefits to participants, public finances and society? 4) Analysis and Recommendations â the above steps inform the analysis and evaluation to understand to what extent and degree of progress towards the reporting aims are being made, and any recommendations for improvements. The report should, where appropriate, include advice for the SLC for future land market reports.

title: ACE Contract Cleaning Services
description: The University of Edinburghâs Accommodation, Catering and Events (ACE) is seeking contractors for cleaning services to a range of student accommodation. This will include full lease end cleans, with the main periods of peak being May through to September and also a flexible resource for weekly cleans, which are unable to be covered in house. There is also a requirement to support commercial cleaning, including hotels and quick turnaround cleans following overnight stays. The nature of the requirement can lead to extreme periods of peak and a need for flexibility in the pool of resources available across all areas. To support this and attract sufficient competition for all requirements, the University is proposing a lotted framework. Proposed lots are; Lot 1: Lease End Cleaning (Including Specialist Cleaning) â Covers all planned and reactive lease end cleans and allows for specialist cleaning (Including carpet and Upholstery) Maximum 8 suppliers . Lot 1 will require the cleaning of approximately 5817 rooms from June to September and 4698 in September only. Lot 2: Commercial Cleaning â Covers all commercial cleaning. Cleaning on this lot includes hotels and therefore has different requirements to Lots 1 and 3, including the standard. Maximum 3 suppliers. The number of rooms to be cleaned will depend on bookings received. Lot 3: DOMUS Cleaning*: This is a separate lot due to the 24-hour turnaround requirement and the need to service multiple properties across the city within the same day. Properties are typically tenement-style flats (1â7 bedrooms) with a kitchen and shared bathroom(s). Access may involve multiple stair flights, with flats located from ground to fourth floor, and parking is often limited.2 suppliers. Lot 3 will require 885 rooms to be cleaned between May and September (based on 65% occupancy level)

description: The aims of the project are to produce an evaluation of the SLCâs rural land market reporting to generate insights and improvements for future reporting. title: Sääsuojaratkaisu rakennustyömaalle
description: Sääsuojaratkaisu rakennustyömaalle Raision seudun koulutuskuntayhtymä pyytää tarjouksia Rasekon ammattiopiston rakennustyömaille hankittavasta uudesta ja käyttämättömästä rakennuksen sääsuojaratkaisusta. Hankinnan kohteena on talon rakentamisvaiheessa käytettävä sääsuojaratkaisu, jonka avulla turvataan työskentelyolosuhteet, rakenteiden kuivana pysyminen sekä rakennusprosessin laatu vaihtelevissa sääolosuhteissa. Sääsuojaratkaisua käytetään oppilaitoksen opetustyömailla, joissa rakennusalan opiskelijat toteuttavat pientalorakentamista osana koulutustaan. Ratkaisun tulee soveltua opetuskäyttöön sekä olla turvallinen ja helppokäyttöinen. Hankittavan sääsuojaratkaisun tulee: - Soveltua liitteessä 3 esitetyn rakennuksen suojaamiseen. - Olla yhteensopiva olemassa olevien Layher-telineiden kanssa. - Sisältää rakennuksen pitkille sivuille tulevat osat (poislukien ulkoneva katos) sekä kattorakenteen. Sääsuojaratkaisun päädyt toteutetaan Rasekon ammattiopiston olemassa olevilla Layher-telineosilla. Tarjottavan sääsuojaratkaisun tulee soveltua pientalokohteiden eri rakentamisvaiheisiin (runko-, julkisivu- ja vesikattovaihe) sekä kestää tavanomaiset suomalaiset sääolosuhteet, kuten tuuli-, sade- ja lumikuormat. Toimitus: Hankinnan kohteena oleva sääsuojaratkaisu tulee toimittaa viimeistään 15.12.2026. Toimituksen tulee sisältää kaikki hankinnan kohteeseen kuuluvat osat siten, että sääsuojaratkaisu on käyttöönotettavissa toimituksen jälkeen ilman olennaisia lisähankintoja. Hankinnan tavoitteena on parantaa työturvallisuutta, rakentamisen laatua sekä opetuksen sujuvuutta. Hankinnan kohde kuvataan tarkemmin tässä tarjouspyynnössä liitteineen. title: Kotiin annettavat turvalaitteet, hälytysten vastaanottopalvelu ja hälytysten vastaanottojärjestelmä
description: Kotiin annettavat turvalaitteet, hälytysten vastaanottopalvelu ja hälytysten vastaanottojärjestelmä Lapin hyvinvointialue pyytää tarjouksia kokonaisuudesta, johon sisältyvät: 1. kotiin annettavat turvalaitteet Lapin hyvinvointialueen asiakkaille 2. hälytysten vastaanottopalvelu 3. hälytysten vastaanottojärjestelmä edellä mainitun palvelun tuottamiseen hyvinvointialueen omana toimintana. Hankinnassa turvalaitteilla tarkoitetaan erilaisia kotiin annettavia turvalaitteita, joilla voidaan parantaa kotona asuvan asiakkaan turvallisuutta. Hankittavia turvalaitteita ovat turvapuhelimet ja niiden lisälaitteet, paikantava turvaranneke sekä ratkaisu yhteisöllisen asumisen ovivalvontaan. Hälytysten vastaanottopalvelulla tarkoitetaan palvelua, jossa otetaan vastaan turvalaitteiden kautta tulevat hälytykset, tehdään alustavan arvion avuntarpeesta ja välitetään pyyntö edelleen turva-auttajille. Palvelun tulee toiminnassa vuorokauden ympäri vuoden jokaisena päivä. Hälytysten vastaanottojärjestelmällä tarkoitetaan järjestelmää, jolla tilaaja voi ottaa eri turvalaitteiden hälytykset vastaan ja edelleenvälittää ne tehtävänä turva-auttajille. Lapin hyvinvointialueella on tarkoitus ottaa hälytysten vastaanottopalvelu omaksi toiminnaksi alustavan aikataulun mukaan keväällä 2028. Hyvinvointialue hankkii hälytysten vastaanottopalvelua siihen asti, kunnes vastaanottojärjestelmä on otettu käyttöön, minkä jälkeen vastaanottopalvelun hankinta päättyy. Hankinnan kohde on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnössä ja sen liitteissä, erityisesti liitteessä 1 "Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus". Kilpailutuksessa valitaan yksi toimitta puitesopimustoimittajaksi. Puitejärjestelyn kautta hyvinvointialue hankkii valitulta toimittajalta turvalaitteita ja palveluita sopimuskauden aikana tarpeen mukaan. Hyvinvointialueen tarpeet voivat vaihdella sopimuskauden aikana, eikä tarjouspyynnöllä sitouduta tiettyihin hankintamääriin. Puitesopimuksen sopimuskausi on määräaikaisena kaksi vuotta, jonka jälkeen sopimus jatkuu toistaiseksi voimassa olevana. Hankintayksikön tarkoitus on tehdä sopimus valitun toimittajan kanssa heti, kun tarjousaika on päättynyt, tarjoukset on vertailtu, hankintapäätös on tehty ja muutoksenhakuaika on päättynyt. Hankintayksikön arvion mukaan ajankohta on lokakuun 2026 aikana. Laitevaihtojen toteutuksen ja muiden käyttöönottoon liittyvien toimien aikataulut sovitaan yhdessä valitun toimittajan kanssa molempien osapuolten tarpeet huomioivalla tavalla. Lisäksi valitulta toimittajalta hankitaan hälytysten vastaanottojärjestelmä kokonaisuutena, johon sisältyy järjestelmän toimittaminen ja sen jatkuva palvelu. Järjestelmän jatkuvan palvelun sopimus on voimassa toistaiseksi. Hankintaa ei ole jaettu osiin, koska kyseessä on yhtenäinen tavaroiden ja palveluiden muodostama kokonaisuus, jonka kaikkien osasten yhteensopivuus on voitava varmistaa. Lapin hyvinvointialueen asiakkaiden turvallisuuden kannalta on tärkeää, että yksi toimittaja vastaa koko kokonaisuuden toimivuudesta. Hankintailmoitus on julkaistu toisen kerran uudelleen, koska kaksi aiempaa hankintamenettelyä on täytynyt keskeyttää hankinta-asiakirjojen muutostarpeiden vuoksi.,

title: Memorialinio kūrinio Klaipėdos miesto įkūrėjams įamžinti sukūrimo ir pastatymo projekto konkursas. (ATVIRAS PROJEKTO KONKURSAS)
description: Memorialinio kūrinio Klaipėdos miesto įkūrėjams įamžinti sukūrimo ir pastatymo projektas. Projekto konkurso dalyviai turi pateikti memorialinio kūrinio meninę idėją, atspindinčią Klaipėdos miesto įkūrimo istoriją, miesto tapatybę ir istorinę atmintį. Projektas turi apimti memorialinio kūrinio meninius, architektūrinius ir techninius sprendinius, jo integravimą į pasirinktą vietą. Kartu turi būti pateikti memorialinio kūrinio vizualiniai, konstrukciniai, medžiagiškumo ir apšvietimo sprendiniai. Su projekto konkurso laimėtoju numatoma sudaryti paslaugų pirkimo–pardavimo sutartį (toliau – projekto (paslaugų pirkimo–pardavimo) sutartis) dėl memorialinio kūrinio projektavimo, pagaminimo, pastatymo ir kitų su projekto įgyvendinimu susijusių darbų atlikimo. Išsamus projekto konkurso objekto aprašymas ir memorialiniam kūriniui keliami reikalavimai pateikiami Techninėje specifikacijoje (konkurso sąlygų 4 priedas). Projekto konkurso tikslas – atrinkti meniškai vertingiausią, istoriškai pagrįstą ir urbanistiniame kontekste tinkamiausią memorialinio kūrinio idėją, skirtą Klaipėdos miesto įkūrėjų atminimui įamžinti ir Klaipėdos miesto istorinės atminties puoselėjimui. Biudžetas: Perkančioji organizacija informuoja, kad memorialinio kūrinio projektavimo, pagaminimo, transportavimo, montavimo bei kitų su projekto įgyvendinimu susijusių paslaugų bendra kaina negali viršyti šiam projekto konkursui skirtos maksimalios sumos – t. y. 123 966,94 Eur be PVM (jei tiekėjas yra ne PVM mokėtojas ar paslaugos neapmokestinamos PVM, ar dėl kitų priežasčių Perkančiosios organizacijos galutinė tiekėjui mokėtina suma bus be PVM) arba 150 000,00 Eur su PVM. Svarbu: jeigu dalyvio pasiūlyta kaina bus didesnė nei šiame punkte nustatyta maksimali kaina, projektas bus atmestas kaip neatitinkantis konkurso dokumentų reikalavimų pagal projekto konkurso sąlygų 64.3 p. Projekto konkurso pirmąsias 3 vietas užėmusius dalyvius numatyta apdovanoti piniginiais prizais (premijomis). Perkančioji organizacija laimėjusiu nustato tik 1 (vieną) dalyvį, surinkusį daugiausiai balų ir esantį pirmoje vietoje, neatitikusį pašalinimo pagrindų ir atitikusį nustatytus kvalifikacijos reikalavimus.

title: Specialized Research Support Services
description: The National Institutes of Health (NIH) intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price Purchase Order to KEMRI-Wellcome Trust Research Programme for Specialized Research Support Services in support of the Kwashiorkor Collaboration Network ("KwashNet"). The Government intends to solicit from a single source in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. The Government anticipates awarding a firm-fixed-price purchase order for specialized research support services, including participant data collection and management, biological sample processing, DNA extraction and quantification, sample shipment to NIH, and scientific consultation in support of an international genomic study of severe acute malnutrition (SAM). The Contractor shall provide personnel with the specialized qualifications and experience necessary to perform the required work. The anticipated level of effort includes: Study Coordinator � 10% Effort The Study Coordinator shall directly manage participant data and biological sample collection activities, including data quality assurance and coordination of study activities. Laboratory Technician � 100% Effort The Laboratory Technician shall perform DNA isolation and quantification from a minimum of 6,000 biological samples, including samples from kwashiorkor/marasmic-kwashiorkor cases and marasmus controls. Project Administrator � 10% Effort The Project Administrator shall support study logistics, procurement activities, staff management, invoices and payments, and other administrative requirements associated with performance of the project. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source because the required services can be provided by only one responsible source capable of satisfying the Government's requirements. The requirement is highly specialized and is directly dependent upon the Contractor's established research infrastructure, access to the existing biorepository and associated electronic records in Kilifi, Kenya, established relationships with the relevant study population, and specialized scientific expertise concerning severe childhood malnutrition, including kwashiorkor, marasmus, marasmic-kwashiorkor, and Kenyan populations. The proposed Contractor's designated Kenya Principal Investigator (PI) and research team possess specialized subject-matter expertise in kwashiorkor, marasmus, and the relevant Kenyan study population and have access to the existing biological samples, participant records, and associated research infrastructure necessary to execute the required work. The Government requires the Contractor to obtain and process samples from the existing population and associated biorepository records rather than establish a new population, develop new biorepository infrastructure, or independently recreate the historical medical and anthropometric information required for this study. The use of an alternative source would require establishing new participant recruitment and research infrastructure and would not provide the same access to the existing cohort, records, biological materials, historical data, and population-specific expertise necessary to meet the Government's scientific objectives within the required period of performance. Additionally, the Kenya PI's specialized knowledge of the study population is necessary to support interpretation of the research findings and appropriate dissemination of pooled, de-identified results to the affected population in Kenya in accordance with local and cultural expectations. Accordingly, the Government has determined that the proposed source is uniquely positioned to satisfy the requirement and that no other responsible source is expected to satisfy the Government's requirements without substantial duplication of effort, delay, and/or unacceptable impact on the scientific integrity and objectives of the study. Therefore, the Government intends to award this requirement on a sole-source basis pursuant to FAR 6.302-1. This notice is not a request for competitive quotations. However, interested parties that believe they can meet the Government's requirements may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide the required services and satisfy all specified technical and operational requirements. The Government will consider all timely capability statements received and determine whether the acquisition should proceed as a sole-source procurement or be competed. The Government anticipates making an award approximately five (5) calendar days after the closing date of this notice, unless the Government determines that another responsible source is capable of meeting the requirement. Capability statements shall be submitted electronically to haunp@mail.nih.gov no later than 9:00 a.m. EDT on September 18, 2026. Please reference Notice No. 75N98026Q01186 in the subject line of the response.

These weirs are designed as an upstream-pointing arch with side slopes which concentrate the flow towards the center of the channel. Further design elements include a 4-foot-wide V-notch in the weir and 1.5-foot diameter boulders emplaced on the weir. The 31st weir (upstream most weir) will be constructed entirely of concrete the intent is to protect the less robust rock emplacements by breaking up incoming ice. Construction of the fishway will involve partial demolition and excavation of the spillway and underlying bedrock to anchor the fishway to the rock and replace the existing spillway. On the downstream end of the fishway the existing channel will be removed for a length of 150 feet. A four foot-wide embedded low-flow channel in the center of the fishway has been designed to provide sufficient depth of water and flow during normal low flow conditions to allow fish passage. A series of parallel transverse rock ridges that consist of 1�6� foot diameter stones will be evenly spaced along the length of the ramp to provide a series of pools and falls. This low-flow channel and rock ridges are designed to allow for the passage of fish and other aquatic life would occur. title: Laser Capture Microdissection Microscope System
description: FAR 6.302-1 � Only One Responsible Source Solicitation Number 75N98026Q01125 Title Accuva Cellect Laser Capture Microdissection (LCM) System Description of Requirement The National Institutes of Health intends to award a contract to Laxco, Inc. on a sole-source basis pursuant to FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements, for the acquisition of an Accuva Cellect Laser Capture Microdissection (LCM) system, including associated software, equipment, installation, training, and support, as applicable. The Accuva Cellect LCM is required to support the Government's established laser capture microdissection research activities. The system must provide specialized capabilities for performing complex laser capture microdissections involving large numbers of regions of interest (ROIs), extensive freehand markup and editing, and selective capture and cutting of individually identified objects or groups. The Accuva Cellect LCM was developed as the successor to the Arcturus XT LCM system, which was discontinued in 2024. The Accuva Cellect retains the software environment and workflow characteristics necessary to support the Government's established LCM procedures. Specific Technical Requirements The required LCM system must provide the following capabilities: Large-Scale ROI Management: The ability to create, manipulate, retain, and process a large number of regions of interest during complex laser capture microdissection procedures without significant loss of system performance. Advanced Freehand Markup Editing: The ability to continuously edit freehand markings, including partial erasure of an existing markup and smooth continuation of the same markup. Selective Object and Group Capture: The ability to individually select objects or groups of objects for capture and/or cutting while retaining a large number of other existing markups. Retention of Complex Markups: The ability to maintain extensive numbers of ROIs and markups while performing additional selections, edits, captures, and cuts within the same workflow. System Stability During Complex Workflows: The ability to perform the foregoing operations without repeated freezing or other interruptions that require the user to reconstruct or substantially modify the LCM workflow. Established Workflow Compatibility: The ability to support the Government's existing research protocols and workflows based on the software and functionality associated with the Arcturus XT LCM platform. Pursuant to FAR 6.302-1, the Government intends to solicit and award a Purchase Order on a sole-source basis because the Government's minimum technical requirements can only be satisfied by the Accuva Cellect LCM system manufactured and supplied by Laxco, Inc. The Government's requirement is based upon specific functional capabilities necessary to perform complex laser capture microdissection procedures. These capabilities are not simply general LCM functions; they involve the ability to efficiently manage large numbers of ROIs and markups, continuously edit freehand markings, selectively capture or cut individually identified objects or groups, and retain extensive markup information throughout the procedure. Based on the Government's market research and knowledge of available LCM systems, Laxco, Inc. is the only known responsible source capable of providing a system that satisfies all of the Government's stated technical requirements. Accordingly, the Government intends to award a sole-source contract to Laxco, Inc. pursuant to FAR 6.302-1. This notice is not a request for competitive quotations. However, interested parties that believe they can meet the Government's requirements may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide the required supplies and meet all specified technical and operational requirements. The Government will consider all timely capability statements received and determine whether the acquisition should proceed as a sole-source procurement or be competed. The Government anticipates making an award approximately five (5) calendar days after the closing date of this notice, unless the Government determines that another responsible source is capable of meeting the requirement. Capability statements shall be submitted electronically to davisroshonna@mail.nih.gov no later than 9:00 a.m. EDT on September 21, 2026. Please reference Notice No. 75N98026Q01125 in the subject line of the response.

title: Legal and Strategic Advisory Services Refresh / On-Ramping #01
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation and request for proposals (RFP) for commercial products or commercial services in accordance with the procedures of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) part 12 - Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services and FAR part 15 - Contracting by Negotiation. Specifically, the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) is issuing this RFP in accordance with Attachment A, Performance Work Statement (PWS), Section 25, �On-Ramping and Refresh of [Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity] IDIQ Holders,� which states, �the Government retains the unilateral right, at any time during the ordering period of this IDIQ contract, to issue additional solicitations and award new IDIQ contracts for the same or substantially similar scope of work to refresh, expand, or otherwise ensure an adequate pool of qualified contractors.� FHFA issued previous RFP FHF-26-R-0032 for �Legal and Strategic Advisory Services,� which resulted in award of six (6) multiple-award IDIQ contracts: 95314326D0002 (ARNOLD & PORTER KAYE SCHOLER LLP) 95314326D0003 (BAKER & HOSTETLER LLP) 95314326D0004 (COHEN SEGLIAS PALLAS GREENHALL & FURMAN PC) 95314326D0005 (DUANE MORRIS LLP) 95314326D0006 (MAYNARD NEXSEN P.C) 95314326D0007 (MINTZ, LEVIN, COHN, FERRIS, GLOVSKY AND POPEO, P.C.) As a result of this Refresh / On-Ramping RFP, FHFA anticipates awarding multiple (likely no more than three (3)) IDIQ contract(s) with an ordering period from effective date of award to 07/26/2031, with the ability for task order performance to extend beyond that date in accordance with applicable terms and procedures. FHFA reserves the unilateral right to award no new IDIQ contracts under this Refresh / On-Ramping RFP. In the event FHFA awards IDIQ contracts as a result of this Refresh / On-Ramping RFP, the IDIQ contracts awarded will be incorporated into the existing multiple-award IDIQ contract vehicle and be eligible to compete for task orders as of the effective date of the award. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation with offers requested. FHFA has a requirement for law firms to provide legal and strategic advisory services to FHFA, which may include but are not limited to: litigation at the state and federal level; oversight and coordination of legal strategy; advice on policy decision making; regulatory advice with respect to the Regulated Entities, the Office of Finance, and U.S. FinTech LLC; significant experience with the Housing and Economic Recovery Act of 2008; legal advice in the areas of banking law, securities law, financial services regulation law; significant experience with the requirements of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act, bankruptcy law, real estate law, antitrust law, administrative law, corporate law (including matters involving boards of directors and governance), insurance law, conservatorships and receiverships of financial institutions, insolvency law, artificial intelligence, privacy law (including but not limited to Privacy Act and Freedom of Information Act matters), internal operations, and other areas of law as needed. A significant portion of the work under these contracts is anticipated to be litigation related, both at the trial court and appellate levels. Litigation services may include, but are not limited to, investigations relating to fraud or other matters; multifamily and single-family real estate matters such as foreclosures, receiverships, or lien priority; federal, state, and local actions that may involve fines, fees, or penalties; issues that may arise related to the conservatorships of Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac; and other litigation or legal advice concerning matters related to the Regulated Entities, the Office of Finance, and U.S. FinTech, LLC. For litigation services, the Contractor shall also provide, as directed by FHFA, court reporting, videography, electronic discovery, exhibit preparation, and expert consultants/witnesses, and any other litigation related services as needed, including administrative and operational support services to support the representation of FHFA. In addition to litigation related issues, contractors are sought for non-litigation areas of legal practice to provide legal advice, analysis, and fact-finding, if appropriate, that are related to the areas of expertise described above. Please refer to Attachment A, PWS, for additional information. Questions or other suggested changes must be submitted via email to Steven Novotny, FHFA Contracting Officer, at Steven.Novotny@fhfa.gov by 9:00 a.m. Eastern on September 15, 2026. Offerors must use Attachment E to organize and submit their questions. The Phase I submission is due no later than the date and time identified on the Contract Opportunities webpage. Please refer to the attachments for additional information.

Step 2: Read the Call for Proposals : https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 Step 3: Propose your solution here : https://can01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fised-isde.canada.ca%2Fsite%2Finnovative-solutions-canada%2Fen%2Fminerva-initiative-uncrewed-ground-system-tactical-cargo-movement%3FauHash%3DjEmyLeYChPKMWuBk0w5wVRVwGOjJaAWVkXdbU8vCpDs&data=05%7C02%7CMikael.Thivierge%40tpsgc-pwgsc.gc.ca%7Cca80e875849f4ea6d08a08defedb028a%7Ce0d54a3c7bbe4a649d46f9f84a41c833%7C0%7C0%7C639228414672791749%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=OZSgLbrhoOrnfoBAlHWnEW%2BaXJeUQy8goDGjyDEXT%2BU%3D&reserved=0 Challenge title: MINERVA Initiative – Uncrewed Ground System for Tactical Cargo Movement Challenge sponsor: Department of National Defense (DND) The Department of National Defence (DND) and the Canadian Army (CA) requires an uncrewed ground system (UGS) to conduct ground delivery of cargo and munitions that is domestically produced, easy to operate and maintain, and adequately rugged to enable the Canadian soldier to successfully fight and survive on the future battlefield. Challenge sponsor: Department of National Defense (DND) Funding mechanism: Contract Opening date: August 24, 2026 Closing date: September 21, 2026, 14:00 Eastern time Challenge Problem statement The CA soldier will face an increasingly complex and dangerous battlespace in the future. A major element of the complexity and danger is the proliferation of multi-spectral sensors and precision weapons that will limit the CA’s ability to move cargo and strike enemy targets at range by using attritable ballistic trajectory weapons without the risk of being targeted and attacked. The CA presently lacks an UGS capable of conducting short-range cargo delivery of light supplies or remote munitions drops. The CA requires an innovative cargo UGS that provides an uncrewed alternative to move combat supplies forward towards the frontline and to deliver munitions independent of predictable ballistic trajectories and large visual signatures. This innovation must be simple, durable, and highly survivable, providing soldiers with an effective capability for future conflicts that integrates seamlessly into operations while minimizing training and maintenance requirements, allowing soldiers to focus on their mission. Desired outcomes and considerations Essential (mandatory) outcomes The proposed solution must: 1. Be composed of a : a. Ground Vehicle: The vehicle containing the onboard electronics, propulsion, and payload. b. Sensor Payload: The equipment required for navigation and to complete a mission, such as cameras or imaging systems. c. Ground Control Station (GCS): The system used by the human operator to control the vehicle and manage missions. Example of GCS components includes without limitation, laptop, tablet, handheld controller, etc. d. Radio: The wireless system that connects the GCS to the UGS to transmit commands and receive telemetry/ data. e. Battery with Charger: A battery for the UGS and a battery charger capable of charging multiple batteries simultaneously. f. Remote antenna: An external antenna placed 100m from the GCS to enhance signal strength, reduce interference, and extend operational range. 2. Operate in a temperature range of -20°C and +40°C. 3. Have a maximum weigh of 410kg in an unladen state. 4. Have a minimum operational radius of 5km (unladen) from the GCS while maintaining user control and live video via Radio Frequency link. 5. Have a minimum operational radius of 10km (unladen) while operating autonomously. 6. Operate at a minimum speed of 15km/hr and a minimum endurance of 4hrs in continuous motion while in an unladen state. 7. Be able to tow a load of 275kg. 8. Be able to carry a load of 140kg onboard the ground vehicle. 9. Be able to carry a tri-wall cargo container measuring 122cm (length) x 102cm (width) x 92cm (height) onboard the ground vehicle. 10. Be capable of navigating paved roads, sand trails, and gravel trails during both day and night at a minimum gradient of 15 degrees (approach and lateral). 11. Have sustained mobility of =7 km/h across while carrying its rated payload across roads, trails, and cross-country terrain. The vehicle must ascend 20% grades, traverse 15% side slopes, negotiate a 250 mm vertical step, and cross a 500 m trench. Additional outcomes The proposed solution should: 1. Be deployable from a stowed state to a mission-ready state in 30 minutes or less. This includes the completion of all pre-mission preparation activities, including but not limited to unstrapping/unloading vehicle, loading/fueling the power system and loading/configuring mission set, resulting in a vehicle that is fully mission-ready at the line of departure. 2. Be appropriately sized such that a minimum of two UGS are stowable for transport on a standard palletized loading system (PLS) deck of 2.44 m x 6.10 m (8 feet wide by 20 feet long). 3. Be capable of operating via fibre-optic cable or other non-electromagnetic (non-EM) communications, enabling operator control from at least 100 m from the vehicle. 4. be powered by electric or hybrid engines; 5. incorporate front automated obstacle avoidance features; 6. emit no more than 5 decibels Sound Pressure Level (dB SPL) of noise in all frequency ranges, measured at a 500m distance from the vehicle; 7. Be recoverable by a North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO)-standard tow hook. 8. Have an aggregated projected production cost of $150,000 CAD or less per system. 9. Have a Ground Control Station (GCS) that: a. Incorporates a simulation capability for Mission Planning. b. Has a minimum remote antenna cable length of 50m. c. Enables UGS navigation via both direct operator control and autonomously using waypoint navigation via the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS). d. Displays the following information: - Location of vehicle in 6 figure Military Grid Reference System (MGRS); - Orientation of vehicle (pitch/roll/yaw); - Point of aim of camera in 6 figure MGRS; - Real-time full motion video feed; and - Battery life. e. Is capable of interfacing with the Tactical Assault Kit (TAK) battle management system to push uncrewed aircraft system (UAS) Position Location Information (PLI) and target PLI. f. Is able to direct the vehicle to return to a pre-determined location in case of loss of link. 10. Demonstrate capacity in having its critical components produced and sourced in countries within the NATO alliance, NATO Partners or Major Non-NATO All

Remote antenna: An external antenna placed 100m away from the GCS to enhance signal strength, reduce interference, and extend operational range. 2. Operate in various weather conditions. At a minimum: a. Operate in a temperature range of -20°C and +40°C; b. Operate in wind speed of up to 40 km/hr; and c. Operate in light rain or snow 0.5mm/m²/hr. 3. Have both a minimum operational radius of 6km and a minimum endurance of 60 min in continuous movement. 4. Have a sensor that enables the operator to recognize a target at a minimum distance under the following conditions: a. Day – Person (180cm) at 0.5km, Vehicle (5m x 3m x 2m) at 1km b. Night – Person (180cm) at 0.25km, Vehicle (5m x 3m x 2m) at 0.5km 5. Have vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) capability in a maximum area of 2m². 6. Be stowable in a 70-litre pack. 7. Be capable of operating at a minimum operational altitude of 1000 feet Above ground Level (AGL). Additional outcomes The proposed solution should: 1. Be deployable from a stowed state to mission-ready state in 10 minutes or less. This includes the completion of all pre-mission preparation activities, including but not limited to unloading vehicle, loading/fueling the power system and loading/configuring mission set, resulting in a vehicle that is fully mission-ready such at the line of departure. 2. Have a maximum takeoff weight of 5kg. 3. Emit no more than 5 decibels Sound Pressure Level (dB SPL) of noise in all frequency ranges, measured at a 500m distance from the UAS. 4. Be capable of operating with fibre-optic wire, or other non-Electromagnetic (EM) spectrum means. 5. Return to a pre-determined location, hover/loiter, and/or climb in case of loss of link. 6. Have an aggregated projected production cost of $40,000 CAD or less per system. 7. Have a Ground Control Station (GCS) that: a. Incorporates a simulation capability for Mission Planning. b. Has a minimum remote antenna cable length of 50m. c. Enables UAS navigation via both direct operator control and autonomously using waypoint navigation via the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS). d. Displays the following information: - Location of vehicle in 6 figure Military Grid Reference System (MGRS); - Orientation of vehicle (pitch/roll/yaw); - Point of aim of camera in 6 figure MGRS; - Real-time full motion video feed; - Altitude in Metres above Sea Level (MSL); and - Battery life. e. Is capable of interfacing with the Tactical Assault Kit (TAK) battle management system to push UAS Position Location Information (PLI) and target PLI. 8. Have an alternate non-electric or hybrid power system capable of sustained operation beyond battery power (i.e. a gas-powered system or a gas/electric hybrid power system). 9. Demonstrate capacity in having its critical components produced and sourced in countries within the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) alliance, NATO Partners or Major Non-NATO Allies . title: Spectrum Auction Verification Services for the mmWave Auction
description: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) is seeking an independent contractor to verify that the Power Auctions software correctly implements the final auction rules in accordance with the Policy and Licensing Framework for Spectrum in the 26 GHz and 38 GHz Bands for determining winning bidders and the prices they will pay. The contractor will develop and implement software based on the rules for the mmWave auction. The contractor will use this software to test and validate the Power Auctions software during the acceptance testing process in advance of the auction, as well as to verify the final allocation of the auction results. If a discrepancy is detected between Power Auctions' and the contractor's software, the contractor will work with ISED to identify the cause of the discrepancy and recommend and assist in implementing a solution. title: Mobile Treatment Center
description: NOTICE OF PROPOSED PROCUREMENT (NPP) The Department of National Defence (DND), in support of the Canadian Forces Health Services (CFHS), has a requirement for the supply, delivery, installation, testing, commissioning, documentation, and warranty support of ten (10) Mobile Treatment Centre (MTC) cap-style slide-in modules. The MTCs will be installed on Government-owned 2024 Dodge RAM 3500 trucks and will provide enhanced casualty treatment, extraction, and transportation capabilities to support CFHS training, routine operations, mandated safety activities, and domestic response operations across Canada. The requirement includes all associated equipment, components, installation harnesses, medical treatment accommodations, electrical and environmental systems, emergency warning equipment, documentation, training, and services necessary to deliver a fully operational capability. The resulting contract will be effective from the date of contract award until March 31, 2028. The initial requirement includes the firm supply, delivery, installation, testing, and commissioning of two (2) Mobile Treatment Centre (MTC) units. Canada will have the option to acquire up to eight (8) additional MTC units, which may be exercised, in whole or in part, at any time during the two-year contract period. Delivery and installation are required at the locations identified in Appendix 1 to Annex Statement of Requirements. Offers will be evaluated in accordance with the evaluation criteria set out in the solicitation documents. The contract will be awarded to the responsive Offeror whose Offer achieves the highest combined rating of technical merit and price. The requirement is subject to the Interim Policy on Reciprocal Procurement. Supplier eligibility will be determined in accordance with the requirements set out in the solicitation documents. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. NOTE TO BIDDERS: Procurement Assistance Canada offers seminars to businesses interested in learning how to sell goods and services to the Government of Canada. The seminars are FREE.

title: VA Magnetic Resonance Safety Expert Services
description: The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Midwest Consortium (MIDCON) has a need for contracted Magnetic Resonance Safety Expert (MRSE) virtual coverage. The contractor shall provide virtual support for participating sites for MRSE assistance and guidance in the MIDCON area, Veterans Integrated Services network (VISNs 15 and 23). The contractor shall provide non-personal, non-inherently governmental services in support of magnetic resonance safety at an all-inclusive price. Contractor and contractor personnel shall not be designated as government officials nor make any inherent governmental decisions. Contractor personnel may not supervise or otherwise direct Government employees. The contractor shall support all participating sites in their Magnetic Resonance Safety needs. A comprehensive list of actual requirements will be included in the Performance Work Statement and within the solicitation package document. The period of performance for this requirement consists of five (5) one (1) year ordering periods. The NAICS code for this procurement is 541690, Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services and the Small Business Administration (SBA) size standard for this requirement is 19 Millon. The proposed requirement action is being set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs). Any vendor desiring to be considered for award MUST also be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) using NAICS code 541690 or a NAICS code with an equivalent size standard. No award can be made unless the vendor is registered in SAM. For additional information and to register in SAM, please access the following web site: www.sam.gov. In order to register with the SAM and to be eligible to receive an award from this acquisition office, all offerors must also have a Unique Entity ID Number. This procurement also requires offerors to complete the electronic representations and certifications at the SAM website. The Government intends to award one (1) firm-fixed price Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity contract. Solicitation documents will be made available for download on or about September 11th, 2026 at https://beta.sam.gov. Paper copies of this solicitation will not be issued. Each potential quoter is responsible for checking the website to gain all current information related to the solicitation. The solicitation and any further announcements regarding the solicitation will be posted only at https://beta.sam.gov. The date proposals are due will be stated within the solicitation documents and will be adjusted based upon the actual release date of the solicitation.

title: REPAIR LIVE FIRE TRAINING FACILITY AIRCRAFT MOCK-UP
description: The 910th Airlift Wing requires repair and corrective work to the Aircraft Fire Training Facility (AFTF) aircraft mock-up located at Youngstown Air Reserve Station. An inspection and evaluation of the Aircraft Fire Training Facility was conducted in August 2025 and finalized in April 2026. The assessment identified deficiencies affecting the facility's burner and ignition systems, structural components, corrosion protection, sprinkler system, propane distribution and emergency shutoff systems, control systems, and associated components. The contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, tools, transportation, testing, quality control, and other items and services necessary to complete the work identified in the Statement of Work, drawings, specifications, and solicitation attachments. Troubleshooting, repair, and/or replacement of the Tail Engine Burner, Wheel Well Burner, Flight Deck Burner, and Cargo Area Burner and associated ignition systems. Repair or replacement of burner ignition components as required to restore proper operation. Replacement of the malfunctioning cargo-area sprinkler head and restoration of proper drainage functionality. Structural steel repairs and corrosion remediation beneath portions of the aircraft mock-up. Corrosion repair beneath flight-deck stairs and around door assemblies. Repair and/or replacement of the warped R2 door and warped grating near the cargo-fire area. Certified welding and associated aircraft mock-up repairs. Installation/restoration of an emergency energy shutoff capability at the propane storage area. Installation of required solenoid valve(s) in the LPG/propane distribution system. Correction of deficiencies involving legacy pneumatic shutoff valves. Required control-system repairs/upgrades. Associated maintenance, testing, and corrective actions necessary to provide a complete and functional system. title: REPAIR LIVE FIRE TRAINING FACILITY AIRCRAFT MOCK-UP
description: The 910th Airlift Wing requires repair and corrective work to the Aircraft Fire Training Facility (AFTF) aircraft mock-up located at Youngstown Air Reserve Station. An inspection and evaluation of the Aircraft Fire Training Facility was conducted in August 2025 and finalized in April 2026. The assessment identified deficiencies affecting the facility's burner and ignition systems, structural components, corrosion protection, sprinkler system, propane distribution and emergency shutoff systems, control systems, and associated components. The contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, tools, transportation, testing, quality control, and other items and services necessary to complete the work identified in the Statement of Work, drawings, specifications, and solicitation attachments. Troubleshooting, repair, and/or replacement of the Tail Engine Burner, Wheel Well Burner, Flight Deck Burner, and Cargo Area Burner and associated ignition systems. Repair or replacement of burner ignition components as required to restore proper operation. Replacement of the malfunctioning cargo-area sprinkler head and restoration of proper drainage functionality. Structural steel repairs and corrosion remediation beneath portions of the aircraft mock-up. Corrosion repair beneath flight-deck stairs and around door assemblies. Repair and/or replacement of the warped R2 door and warped grating near the cargo-fire area. Certified welding and associated aircraft mock-up repairs. Installation/restoration of an emergency energy shutoff capability at the propane storage area. Installation of required solenoid valve(s) in the LPG/propane distribution system. Correction of deficiencies involving legacy pneumatic shutoff valves. Required control-system repairs/upgrades. Associated maintenance, testing, and corrective actions necessary to provide a complete and functional system. Applicable standards identified in the Government's technical documentation include, as applicable: USAF Technical Order 35E1-2-13-1 NFPA 54 NFPA 58 NFPA 70 NFPA 1003 NFPA 1402

description: COMBINED SYNOPSIS AND SOLICITATION REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP) 47QACA26R0306: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. The contract is for a base year and four option years. Task Orders will be issued on a labor-hours (LH) basis using the Contractor�s fully loaded labor-hour rates, applicable labor categories, and required level of effort. This is a 100% set-aside restricted to responsible SBA-certified Women-Owned Small Businesses (WOSB) participating in the WOSB Federal Contract Program. Offerors must be currently certified as WOSBs in the SBA WOSB certification system at the time of proposal submission and at the time of award. (iii) The Contractor shall provide personnel with the ability to augment the SBA's workforce and support OCRM at its Headquarters office in Washington, D.C. Provide assistance with 7(a) loan transfers, invoice resolution, and maintenance of risk identification protocols generation of deliverables to identify SBA Lenders that are, or should be, subject to increased supervision and/or enforcement actions (iv) The anticipated period of performance is October 6, 2026 through October 5, 2027 (not including the four (4) one-year option periods). title: Acquisition for 10X Genomics GEN X Epi Multiome
description: This requirement is for the procurement of proprietary genomics consumables manufactured by 10x Genomics, Inc., including the GEM-X Epi Multiome system and associated kits. The items to be acquired consist of the GEM-X Epi Multiome, 16 samples (Catalog #1000979), GEM-X Epi Multiome Chip Kit, 4 chips (Catalog #1000951), Single Index Kit N Set A (Catalog #1000212), and 10x Magnetic Separator B (1000394). These products are designed specifically for use with 10x Genomics platforms and are required to support multiomic sequencing workflows. The required products must possess specific functional and performance characteristics to meet the Government�s needs. The consumables and associated equipment must be fully compatible with existing 10x Genomics instrumentation and workflows and enable simultaneous epigenomic and transcriptomic profiling from the same biological sample. The system must support high-throughput processing of up to 16 samples per kit and utilize proprietary reagents that ensure data quality and reproducibility. Additionally, the consumables must be single-use, as required by the manufacturer, and designed to integrate seamlessly with existing laboratory protocols without modification. The magnetic separation equipment must be specifically designed for use with 10x Genomics workflows and enable efficient and reliable bead-based separation steps required in the protocol. These characteristics are essential to maintain continuity of ongoing research and ensure accurate and reliable experimental results.

title: CJAG Fence Install
description: Amendment 1 - 10 Sep 2026 - Add POC for site visit, Added drawing, Added Q&A. Site Visits Encouraged - Call to schedule - Call 1SG Brian Persing 614-336-6975 or CW2 Grant Stoner 614-336-6580. Attachment added: 01_SHEETS-FENCE-V3.pdf Q&A Question 1. Gate Configuration: PWS Paragraph 5.1 identifies two 20-foot manual sliding security gates, while Paragraph 5.1.5 references �swing clearance.� Please confirm whether the required gates are manual sliding gates, swing gates, or another configuration. Answer 1. Manual sliding gates Question 2. Field Measurements / Site Access: The PWS requires the contractor to verify all measurements prior to submitting a quotation. Will the Government conduct a scheduled site visit or otherwise provide access to Load Line 6 for prospective contractors to perform the required field verification before the quotation due date? Answer 2. Can either have a scheduled site visit day or be available when needed by appointment with prospective contactors, although until clearing is complete not much to see. Question 3. Fence Alignment / Drawings: Are drawings, site plans, maps, or other documents available identifying the exact proposed fence alignment and locations of the two 20-foot gates? Answer 3. Fence Alignment drawing was provided (also see attached here, once clearing is complete, BDE 12T assets will be used to layout alignment. Question 4. Completion Schedule: The PWS states a six-month period of performance from contract award; however, the solicitation instructions require a proposed schedule demonstrating completion prior to December 1, 2026. Please confirm whether December 1, 2026 is the mandatory completion deadline or whether the contractor will receive six months from the date of award. Answer 4. Complete prior to December 1 is preferred, also cant start until after clearing is complete in late September / October Question 5. Underground Utilities: The PWS directs the contractor to coordinate with CJAG Department of Public Works to locate and mark underground utilities. Will CJAG/DPW perform the utility locating and marking at no cost to the contractor, or should the contractor include any associated utility-locate costs in its quotation? Answer 5. no active utilities in the area Question 6. Permits: Are any local, state, installation, excavation, or construction permits required for this project? If so, please identify which permits the contractor is responsible for obtaining and paying for. Answer 5. This project is covered under the C-JAG Storm Water Construction Permit and the contractor will have to attend a brief training on the SWP3, submit a co-permittee NOI, sign a Contractor certification form, install additional sediment and erosion controls if necessary, comply with fueling requirements and spill kits, comply with concrete outwash, level ruts, prepare seed bed, and seed and straw all bare earth areas they create. Question 7. Site Conditions / Clearing: Can the Government provide additional information or photographs showing the existing conditions along the approximately 3,850-linear-foot fence alignment, particularly the amount of brush, vegetation, grading, or other site preparation anticipated within the required 10-foot-wide clearing corridor? Answer 7. A site visit is authorized Question 8. Excess Soil / Disposal: May excess soil generated from the post-hole excavation be spread or relocated on Government property at a location designated by the COR, or must all excess soil be removed from Camp James A. Garfield and disposed of off-site? Answer 8. Soil can be spread in the clear zone and a seed bed prepared and all bare earth areas seeded with a C-JAG approved turf grass mix and mulched with 2� to 3� of straw cover. Question 9. Installation Access: Is there an anticipated processing timeframe for contractor and subcontractor personnel to obtain installation access/background-check approval? Additionally, are there any vehicle, equipment, escort, or badging requirements bidders should account for when developing their pricing and schedule? Answer 9. An access roster will be provided, valid drivers license or photo ID must be present at all times. Question 10. Wage Requirements: Please confirm whether a Davis-Bacon Act wage determination or any other prevailing-wage requirement applies to this construction requirement. If applicable, please provide or identify the applicable wage determination. Answer 10. Yes Davis-Bacon Act applies. Question 11. Gate Hardware: Please confirm whether there are any specific requirements for gate latches, locking hardware, rollers/tracks, stops, drop rods, or other gate hardware beyond the requirements currently contained in the PWS and applicable UFS/UFC criteria. Answer 11. There are no additional hardware requirements besides those contained in the PWS and UFS. Question 12. Government-Furnished Information: Are there any additional drawings, specifications, site photographs, utility information, or technical documents that will be provided by amendment before quotations are due? Answer 12. No Question 13. What is the Height of the fence? Answer 13. The fence height is 8 feet, with a minimum of 7 feet of fabric plus the top guard outrigger and barbed wire. Question 14. Is the contractor to install a slide gate or swing gate? Answer 14. Slide Gate Question 15. Are the fence and footers to be removed by installation contractor? Answer 15. Old fence will be removed prior to start of work. Question 16. Can the footers and fence be left on site? Answer 16. No Question 17. Does the fence need to be grounded? If so, how often does it need to be grounded? Answer 17. Grounding is not required for this project. Question 18. What your spec on FE-6, we want to make sure we don�t have tension wire, rods, barbed wire on the inside and outside ect. Answer 18. Not sure what the question is. Question 19. Confirm which specific portions of the project require integrated intrusion detection systems (sensored) versus standard perimeter fencing (non-sensored) to select the correct detail (FEN-03 vs. FEN-04). Answer 19. There will be no intrusion detection systems on the fence. Question 20. Review Hardware: High-security specifications (ASTM F626) mandate specific fittings, tension bands, and tie wires. Ensure your material take-off accounts for these high-security grade accessories rather than standard commercial hardware. Answer 20. Not high security specs Question 21. Confirm Gate Requirements: Refer to the FEN-09 detail specifically for any swing or cantilever gates, as these have distinct framing, post size (often 4-inch or 6 5/8-inch OD depending on width), and bracing requirements compared to the main fence line. Answer 21. Manual sliding gates ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Construction of approximately 3,850 linear feet of FE-6 security fencing, including two 20-foot manual security gates, at Load Line 6, Camp James A. Garfield, Ravenna, Ohio Site visits are encouraged - call 1SG Brian Persing 330-984-8130 or CW2 Grant Stoner 614-336-6580. Only contact for site visits, all other questions are submitted to barry.b.beale.civ@army.mil
